A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DP-TTA work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original adaptation accuracy, runtime measurements, ablations, and sensitivity experiments on ImageNet-C, ImageNet-R, and clean ImageNet.

after.justification: The original empirical study is retained, including revised SAR-with-clipping results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the DP-TTA update rules, architecture requirements, and Appendix A variants are unchanged. The revised SAR-with-clipping scores are not accompanied by a documented algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-C, ImageNet-R, and clean ImageNet, retaining the same continual, episodic, and cross-distribution tuning scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the source model, Tent, EATA, SAR, DeYO, DeYO-COME, and their clipping/private variants. The comparator sets in the component and filtering ablations also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported architectures, top-1 accuracy metric, corruption severity, adaptation procedures, tuning grids, and batch-size settings are unchanged. Neither PDF documents a protocol revision explaining the replacement SAR scores.

E4.justification: The existing batch-size sensitivity evidence in Table 11 is revised: SAR + clip now exceeds SAR at all six batch sizes, whereas v1 shows mostly losses. The component ablations, clipping/filtering comparisons, and hyperparameter sensitivity studies otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed accuracy experiments with standard deviations and three-run runtime averages. The revised SAR standard deviations change result values, not the uncertainty-reporting procedure; Figure 1's caption edit retains the same five-seed practice.

E6.justification: Changes are localized to SAR + clip. Under unchanged reported settings, ImageNet-C averages change from 60.5% to 61.7% continually (Tables 1/8) and 62.9% to 64.2% episodically (Tables 6/9), reversing losses against SAR into gains. Table 11 replaces all six batch-size scores, and Table 12 changes ImageNet-R accuracy from 64.0% to 68.0%. Other methods' results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The differential-privacy definition, Proposition 3.1 and its proof, mathematical update rules, and Appendix B.5 privacy-accounting derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: private TTA updates, beneficial per-sample clipping, and characterization of the privacy–accuracy trade-off. Revised SAR results provide different support for an existing claim without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.6 removes the specific explanation that smaller batches cause SAR and SAR + clip to suffer greater noise accumulation. It also removes SAR from the examples of slower-adaptation effects. The broader noise/adaptation trade-off and applicability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract newly provides a code-availability statement and the van-hammerheads/private-stable-tta repository address. Implementation libraries, model identifiers, hyperparameter information, hardware, and runtime documentation otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to prior TTA, differential privacy, and gradient-clipping research are unchanged. Reference pagination changes do not introduce or remove cited work.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits in the introduction and experiments, shortened batch-size discussion, and an additional funding acknowledgement. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 widens its accuracy axis from 55–70% to 50–75% and revises its caption. Table 4 moves from page 9 to page 8, with accompanying text and reference reflow. The figure and table inventory remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new code pointer improves reproducibility guidance, and removing the SAR-specific noise explanation makes Appendix B.6 more cautious. These are limited quality gains. The PDFs do not explain the SAR result replacements, so their higher reported accuracy is not itself evidence of improved experimental validity.
